account:
Today has mostly appeared ordinary, but a vague rumor about bridge or port changes has circulated without anyone identifying an actual proposal. The secretary traced a named link to Townsfolk 03, who directed her to the innkeeper. The innkeeper denied proposing or announcing any change. Our neighbour at the east-bank cottage had also heard a vague version, but gave me no source or specifics. I do not yet know where it began or what purpose, if any, it serves.

The builder reported the bridge passable with no confirmed defects and relayed Freight's report of sound roads and a trouble-free ferry crossing. I authorized no repairs or spending; any genuine maintenance need must receive a written estimate and approval first. The secretary's accounts record says no receipts, claims, or repair contracts have been received. Nothing I have learned establishes a practical reason for the rumor.

At tea, our neighbour described quiet docks, Freight offering ferry rides and deliveries, and the baker preparing ordinary market bread rather than a special celebration. Those are reports, not evidence of a concealed event. The builder came asking about repair needs, and the secretary clarified the cottage location for my appointments. I noticed no unusual activity firsthand that proves people are organizing something without me.

I remain curious rather than convinced of a scheme. I have asked the secretary to arrange a brief conversation with Townsfolk 03 tomorrow, without displacing my appointments, so I can hear the original information directly. She agreed and will have my appointment book ready for morning review. Today's records are back in the office chest. My next scheduled engagement is home at nineteen.
